top.title: Bitcoin Price Fades Near $61,000 as Stocks Soar on Huang’s Return
top.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Fades Near $61,000 as Stocks Soar on Huang’s Return The bitcoin price slipped back to near $61,100 on Monday afternoon, giving up nearly all of its morning spike even as Wall Street held one of its biggest rallies in years on Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. Bitcoin jumped above $64,000 shortly after the Nvidia news broke before 10 a.m. ET and topped out near $64,500. The move reversed within hours , and the bitcoin price dipped to around $60,800 by 2:45 p.m. ET. It remains up only modestly on the day. The round trip was costly for leveraged traders. Bitcoin liquidations reached about $321 million , with short bets making up $224 million of that total. Liquidations across the broader crypto market topped $762 million. Stocks hold gains as bitcoin fades Stocks kept climbing while bitcoin slid. The Nasdaq Composite was up about 6.9% near 24,170 at about 3:40 p.m. ET, while the S&P 500 gained about 5% and the Dow rose about 3.2%. The S&P 500 had fallen seven straight days before Monday. Nvidia (NVDA) led the move, trading near $165.66, up about 32% from Friday’s close of $125.53. The board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, CEO and director, 12 days after he resigned. A stronger dollar may be weighing on the bitcoin price. The dollar index rose about 0.65% to 104.40 , its strongest level since April 2025, as the stock rebound put more Federal Reserve rate hikes back in play. The Fed meets Dec. 8-9, and a quarter-point hike remains the base case. Adam Haeems, head of asset management at Tesseract Group, pointed to steady selling during U.S. market hours since Huang first stepped down. “Bitcoin has fallen in seven of the eight U.S. sessions since Huang went, today’s included, and last week each session’s fall lined up with that day’s ETF outflow,” he said. Crypto stocks keep most of their gains Crypto stocks held up far better than the bitcoin price. Strategy (MSTR) was up about 9.3% near $85.03 in afternoon trading, after it disclosed a purchase of 457 bitcoin last week. Coinbase (COIN) gained about 6.7% to near $108.78, Robinhood (HOOD) rose about 8.8% to near $67.64 and Circle (CRCL) added about 8% to near $51.33. Miners with AI data center businesses posted the biggest moves. IREN (IREN) jumped about 23% to near $14.57, CleanSpark (CLSK) rose about 12.6% and MARA Holdings (MARA) gained about 10%. Core Scientific (CORZ) climbed about 9.4% and Riot Platforms (RIOT) added about 7.1%. ETF flows and inflation data are next Monday’s spot bitcoin ETF flows are the next test. The funds lost about $1.79 billion last week, their fourth straight week of net outflows, as bitcoin slid toward $58,000 on Friday and hit a weekend low near $55,100. “Tonight’s ETF flow figure is the first real test of this bounce,” Haeems said. top.description: Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud (7) is seen during the second half of an NFL football game in Houston, Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026. (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle) It's been 13 months since the Houston Texans last played a game on Monday Night Football, but C.J. Stroud will play a small role in Monday night's broadcast of the Cincinnati Bengals-Washington Commanders game this week. The Texans quarterback will be a guest on the ManningCast of Monday night's game, joining hosts Peyton and Eli Manning on ESPN2's broadcast of the game. The game will be broadcast on ESPN with the traditional crew of Joe Buck and Troy Aikman, but the Mannings on ESPN2 offer a little something different with their own insights into the game as well as a few guests who join remotely. Stroud will be just this season's third active player to appear on The ManningCast, which does 10 regular season Monday night games a year. top.title: Ex-Chelsea star defends Cole Palmer after criticism over reaction to Leeds loss
top.description: Former Chelsea striker Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink has defended Cole Palmer ’s commitment after the forward faced scrutiny following Saturday’s 4-1 thrashing at home against Leeds. Palmer failed to score once again, leaving him with just a single goal across his last nine Premier League appearances during a difficult run for Xabi Alonso ’s side. The England outcast attracted attention after the defeat due to an apparent exchange of words with injured team-mate Joao Pedro near the dugout, while reports suggested the Chelsea playmaker did not acknowledge the frustrated home support at Stamford Bridge . However, Hasselbaink told talkSPORT : "No, I don’t think there is discontent. I think there is a frustration that things are not going the way they want to go and certain individuals deal with that better than others. Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink has defended Palmer (John Walton/PA) (PA Wire) "The expectation is a lot higher than what is being delivered at the minute and that’s from in the camp, but also from outside the camp and let’s not talk about the commitment of Cole Palmer. I don’t think that is the problem. "At the moment you see he is playing different because he is looking for the ball, but looking for the ball way deeper when he should get it way higher. "It’s the midfielders that should find him in a higher position and at the moment the majority of the time he is starting the majority of the play, so he is not playing as high and as much around the box." Following Palmer’s high-profile omission from Thomas Tuchel ’s England squad for the summer World Cup, the 24-year-old launched the new campaign with goals in victories over Fulham and Brighton to help Alonso make a bright start in west London. Palmer’s form has dipped since, however, during a spell in which Tuchel admitted the Chelsea attacker "misses too many opportunities to impress" to earn an international recall. Pressure is building on Xabi Alonso (PA) Alonso and Palmer are both under pressure following a painful first home loss to Leeds in 27 years, which leaves them with five defeats from 11 league fixtures, though Hasselbaink laid the blame on the team as a whole. "When a new manager comes in and especially with the pedigree of Xabi, yeah you think he would make straight away an impact or a big impact but the players are still the same," Hasselbaink said. "Managers do need time to assess things and adjust things, but the same problems keep on occurring at the moment and that’s really the disappointment."

top.title: ‘Tyreek Hill’s back’ – Kansas City Chiefs breakout star reminds me of former wide receiver, says Mike Florio
top.description: Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs’ offense has stepped up a level over the past two weeks, with Patrick Mahomes throwing eight touchdown passes. The running game has also had a different look, rookie Emmett Johnson has stepped into the backfield with Kenneth Walker dealing with an injury. Johnson had 105 rushing yards in Week 11 and one touchdown, plus a further 38 receiving yards from four targets. The rookie wears the Chiefs’ number 10 jersey once worn by wide receiver Tyreek Hill, and Mike Florio sees similarities with his burst of pace. Speaking to Pro Football Talk, Florio explained: “You’ve got to use him. I mean, people see that number 10, and I’ve heard people say it’s Isiah Pacheco. “When I see him running in the open field, I’m thinking Tyreek Hill’s back, it is just the weirdest thing to see. “But he is extremely effective, and there are teams out there kicking themselves that they didn’t draft him when they could.” How Johnson’s 40 yard dash compares to Tyreek Hill Tyreek Hill was also a fifth-round draft pick for the Kansas City Chiefs, 10 years earlier. He went on to win one Super Bowl with Patrick Mahomes, before forcing an exit to sign with the Miami Dolphins. Hill, 32, is attempting to recover from a serious knee injury and wants to revive his NFL career. He was renowned as the fastest player in the NFL, and Florio’s comparison is a major compliment for Emmett Johnson and his own ability to run into space with the ball. Tyreek Hill did not participate at the NFL Combine, but set a 4.29 time at the 40-yard dash at his West Alabama Pro Day. Emmett Johnson’s dash time was an unimpressive 4.56 seconds, which also helps to explain why he fell to the fifth round. The Chiefs still saw something special in him, and Johnson is proving it on the field where it really matters. The teenager played a decisive role in a result that quickly took shape after Leny Yoro’s early dismissal. Dominik Szoboszlai opened the scoring from the resulting free-kick, Florian Wirtz doubled the lead after excellent work from Ngumoha, and the young forward then capped his afternoon with a goal of his own before Victor Munoz added the fourth late on. For Liverpool, the scoreline reflected control as much as quality. For Ngumoha, it was a significant afternoon in his development, delivering a goal and an assist in a fixture that carries weight regardless of the circumstances. Rio Ngumoha delivers on biggest stage There was an assurance to Ngumoha’s performance that stood out from the outset. Liverpool had prepared during the week without complete clarity over what to expect from United under a new manager, so there was an element of adaptation required in the opening exchanges. Once Yoro saw red, the contest changed, but the task still demanded patience and precision. Ngumoha handled both. His creative contribution for Wirtz’s finish was one of the afternoon’s standout moments, full of awareness and confidence, and his own goal underlined a willingness to attack decisive spaces. That combination of invention and directness gave Liverpool an edge throughout. His post-match message was measured and team-focused, “I just want to help the team as much as I can”, a line that neatly summed up both the maturity of his outlook and the way he approached the game itself. There was further significance in the numbers. Ngumoha became the second-youngest Liverpool player to score and assist in a Premier League match, after Michael Owen, an indicator of the company he has joined, even if the immediate focus inside the camp will remain on performance levels rather than milestones. top.title: 'My football hasn't changed' - Kevin De Bruyne responds to prospect of Man City being stripped of titles as Napoli star returns to the Etihad
top.description: FBL-EUR-C1-NAPOLI-PRESSER - AFP Kevin De Bruyne insists the prospect of Manchester City being stripped of titles would not change how he views his decade at the Etihad Stadium. Back in Manchester with Napoli, the Belgian declared his love for City's owners and admitted "everybody plays on the limit" of the rules, as he prepares to face his former club in the Champions League on Tuesday. De Bruyne responds to title-stripping threat De Bruyne has insisted his achievements with City will not be tarnished if the club are stripped of titles following the Premier League's guilty verdict. City were found guilty in September of the majority of the financial charges against them, and are appealing the decision. Speaking at a press conference at the Etihad on Monday night, De Bruyne was asked about the possibility of losing honours such as the 100-point title of 2017-18. "It still doesn't change, my football hasn't changed. Of course, in life, there are rules but everybody plays on the limit, I'd say," he said. 'I've given my all' The midfielder, who won six Premier League titles during his 10 years at City, insisted that his legacy is secure. "I've given my all, that's not going to change in my mind, I don't think a lot of people would change in their mind how they view me as a player or how we played," he said. "But... Ah! Everybody has their own opinion, I guess, and how people [say] 'disgrace', I can't change anything about that." De Bruyne added that his relationships with team-mates were what he valued most. 'This is my club! I love the owners' The Belgian made it clear that his bond with City remains as strong as ever, despite the verdict. "And honestly I still... This is my club! I love the owners, I've talked about a lot of stuff outside of football, I've even spoken to Khaldoon [Al Mubarak] how to buy a club and everything," he said. "I've nothing but affection for this club and that will never change! Even now, the people who treated me for 10 years exceptionally, my family and everything, that's for me the most important and for me, that is it to be honest." Emotional Etihad return awaits De Bruyne will now face his old club on Tuesday, as Enzo Maresca's side look to end their slump . The 35-year-old also hit out at reports in the Italian press about his future, saying the coverage had led to unpleasant reactions towards his wife.

The Indianapolis Colts have not ruled out Alec Pierce for the remainder of the 2026 season, despite reports suggesting the wide receiver could be done for the year . Head coach Shane Steichen addressed Pierce’s status and pushed back on those reports , making it clear that the team has not made a decision about shutting him down. “I know there’s reports out there on Alec Pierce being done for the season. We have not made that determination,” Steichen said, via ESPN’s Stephen Holder. “He’s still going through his rehab process. The only way we’ll put him out there is if he’s 100%. We gotta be really smart.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Pierce has been sidelined since aggravating his surgically repaired left heel during the Colts’ Week 2 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. Indianapolis placed him on injured reserve in September, and he has yet to establish a timeline for his return. The fifth-year receiver underwent surgery on the same heel and ankle during the offseason before returning for the start of the regular season. Unfortunately, the injury resurfaced just two games into the year, leaving the Colts without one of their top receiving options. While Steichen has not ruled out a return, his comments make it clear that Indianapolis will not rush Pierce back onto the field . The Colts want him fully healthy before considering a return, and there is no guarantee that happens before the end of the season. For now, Pierce remains in the rehab process, and the Colts are leaving the door open for a possible return. Friday’s game is officially sold out. Besides honoring the seniors, Friday is also the 16 th annual Heros Game. Citizen heroes are honored from each state, and UI Athletics has selected Hannah Jorgensen as Iowa’s hero. Hannah, 24, a fifth-grade teacher at Borlaug Elementary School in Coralville, was on a class field trip to the MacBride Nature Recreation Area when a student slipped and fell into the water. Hannah dove into the lake to rescue the student, and unfortunately both lost their lives. At strong safety, Anthony Hawkins is listed as the starter, after Xavier Styles missed last Saturday’s game against Illinois. First year player Marcello Vitti is listed as the backup. Tony Diaz is still listed on the depth chart as the starter. Diaz had been battling soft tissue issues last week (most likely a hamstring), but in Saturday’s game he logged 67 of Iowa’s 78 offensive snaps and was their leading receiver with four catches for 52 yards and added two carries for 21 yards. Center Cael Winter is listed as the starter after he was cleared to return to the lineup last week after he had missed the last two games and played all 78 offensive snaps. Zach Lutmer remains as the listed starter. Lutmer had initially been listed as questionable on the initial injury report last week but then was cleared to play. Lutmer played 58 defensive snaps, tying Anthony Hawkins and Deshaun Lee for the highest snap total in Iowa’s secondary, and finished with five tackles No changes to special teams. Iowa held steady at No. 13 in the AP Top 25 Poll and stands at 9-2 overall and 6-2 in the Big Ten. Nebraska is 7-4 overall and 4-4 in the conference, tied for fourth place in the B1G. On the season in the conference, Nebraska has scored 195 points and has allowed 142 points. Depth Chart Notes Positions listed with OR are ordered numerically. The starting defensive lineup will vary based on formation and personnel packages.

top.title: OVC instruction guide three weeks into the season
top.description: The Ohio Valley Conference is 6-37 against DI opponents this season, entering the start of Feast Week…not exactly the ideal way the conference expected to enter the season, especially when 11 of those losses have been by 10 points or fewer. It’s rough going for a conference that many thought was underrated entering the season, but there are some bright spots in this deep, dark valley up to this point. UT Martin: Heart attack warning The Skyhawks are legitimately three possessions away from 7-0, yet they sit at a respectable 4-3 headed into the final night of the U.S. Virgin Islands Paradise Jam. After seven games of Jeremy Shulman’s team, it is very clear that this is the best team in the OVC. Even though there are plenty of things that need to be polished up before conference play begins, UT Martin boasts wins over Arkansas State and Southern Illinois, with close losses at Tulane, IU Indy, and against Utah Valley, all powered by the star backcourt of Davi Remagen and Kaan Onat. While almost completely different physically, with Remagen relying on his speed and athleticism to blow by defenders and get shots up quickly, and Onat using his strength to methodically break down defenses, the duo have immediately made their names on the national scene. Sasha Savkov as well has been a very important part of their success, using his 6-foot-11 frame and shooting ability to send his team on big runs when needed. Western Illinois: Some assembly required The Leathernecks have opened their season with four losses by eight or fewer points to DI opponents, but a big win over Canisius on Sunday, along with an impressive showing at the Queen City Classic overall, has really proven that Chad Boudreau’s team has some high-level potential if its pieces can fit together. Daivion Traylor has been fantastic through five games, averaging 14.4 points and 7.3 rebounds per outing, and sophomore returner Makai Kvamme has been the quality guard that Boudreau has been looking for, averaging 10.4 points and almost two steals per game. The perimeter defense has been the biggest strength, with WIU forcing teams to a conference-low 25.5% from beyond the arc. Unfortunately, teams are finding ways around that, with the interior defense sitting in the bottom 30 in DI (60.1%FG on two-pointers) While the offense is still truly a work in progress, Western Illinois has the pieces to put themselves in the same position they were in during Boudreau’s first year at the helm just three years ago, when the Leathernecks finished one game back from first in the league. The offense might not wow opponents, but the defense and size can force teams to find a way to win in unorthodox ways, and that is what can give the Leathernecks a chance come conference play. top.title: Breaking down the Sox-Rox trade
top.description: Sean Sullivan is the x-factor in the most recent trade between the White Sox and Rockies. | ﻿(Photo by Norm Hall/Minor League Baseball via Getty Images) On November 19, the White Sox sent Luis Castillo and Davis Martin to the Colorado Rockies in exchange for left-handed pitching prospect Sean Sullivan and 17-year-old catcher Doug Veliz. Let’s break down the exchange and see what Chicago’s plans likely are. On a surface level, this is a better deal for the Rockies. Castillo is a veteran starting pitcher, with a 3.75 career ERA in 266 starts over the last decade. Martin is also an established starter, and 2026 was his career-best season for starts (28), innings pitched (146) and ERA (3.95). He spent the first half of the year as the ace of the White Sox staff, and finished with solid season-long numbers. Meanwhile, Sullivan was Colorado’s No. 10 prospect on MLB Pipeline’s 2025 rankings, making five major league starts in 2026 but was rocked to an 8.87 ERA. Veliz is a teenager whose total pro ball experience is 117 PAs in the Dominican Summer League. So, then, why would the White Sox trade two quality starting pitchers for two prospects, one of whom has already struggled in the big leagues and the other being about as inexperienced as you can get? Well, it’s pretty simple — the trade was a salary dump for Castillo. He’s entering his age-34 season, and struggled substantially in 2026. He had a 5.06 ERA for the Seattle Mariners when the White Sox acquired him at the trade deadline. He proceeded to be even worse for the Sox, posting an 8.42 ERA over six starts. Castillo finished the year with a 5.85 ERA, in 130 2/3 innings over 29 games (23 starts). He’s owed $22.75 million in 2027, with a vesting option for 2028, and was the most expensive player on the Sox payroll. Now, Castillo was much better in 2025 and had been very durable and productive up until 2026, so it’s possible he’ll bounce back next year. But the Sox probably don’t want a 34-year-old starter coming off a career-worst season to be their most expensive player. The Rockies have a track record for taking on aging, veteran pitchers, which made them a good candidate to take on Castillo’s salary. It’s much harder to figure out where Martin fits in. He pitched well for the Sox last year, and he’s not even arbitration-eligible until 2028. While the righthander had a solid 2026 (2.3 bWAR), he had a brutal stretch from June through August — which is a big chunk of the year. Martin was bad and/or hurt enough that he finished up in the bullpen. He also doesn’t have the most successful track record, only pitching partial seasons in 2022 and 2024 (never to great success), while missing most of 2023 to Tommy John surgery, and being lackluster in 2025. top.title: The Grandson of The Greatest: Nico Ali Walsh on Fighting, Loss, and Protecting the Ali Boxing Reform Act
top.description: Nico Ali Walsh (center) testifies at a Senate Committee hearing on federal boxing laws in Washington, DC, April 2026. (Photo by Saul Loeb / AFP via Getty Images) “The nerves reach a peak right before the bell hits,” says Nico Ali Walsh , the bell signaling the suspension of assault laws. When it dings, he and another man are legally free to beat each other in the head and body as hard and fast as possible. It’s a family tradition. More from Spin: Zwan’s ‘Mary Star Of The Sea’ Gets Deluxe Vinyl Reissue Justin Timberlake Confronts His Legacy In Apple TV Doc Trailer Soundwalk Collective, Patti Smith Continue ‘Correspondences’ Nico’s granddad was, of course, the sweet science’s zenith—The Greatest!— Muhammad Ali . So, when a teenage Nico decided to try his hand in the ring, he had a very special oldtimer spurring him on. “We would always watch videos of my sparring,” says Nico. “Every time I didn’t want to keep going, he’d push me to keep going. He wanted me to keep fighting.” Nico was raised (and still lives) in Las Vegas, with Muhammad in the Phoenix area. “My first amateur fight was down the street from him [Ali]. He was sick at the time, so he didn’t make the fight,” says Nico. “The next day I went back to his house and said, ‘Poppy, I lost the fight.’ Then we had a conversation about how losing is an opportunity to come back even better. He motivated me,” says Nico, now 26 and fighting as a middleweight. The determined youngster turned pro at 21. Nico now has 17 pro fights, winning 13 and losing two, with a draw and a no contest. He fought the Thai boxer Kittisak Klinson last year in the Philippines’ iconic Araneta Coliseum, where, 50 years earlier, his grandfather and Joe Frazier fought the Thrilla in Manila. Nico Ali Walsh (at right) in the office with Billy Wagner, Madison Square Garden, 2022. (Photo by Williams Paul/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Another fight he has picked up from his grandpa is the Muhammad Ali Boxing Reform Act . Championed by the Greatest himself, the Act protects boxers’ interests and independence and works against fixed contests, not allowing companies to simultaneously manage fighters, promote fights, and control the ranking and title system. Now, however, a new proposed law disingenuously titled Muhammad Ali American Boxing Revival Act is being pushed by Dana White, whose UFC juggernaut operates as an enclosed system in which fighters lack the independence of boxers. Dead opposite to what Muhammad Ali helped make law. “It’s absolutely horrible for boxing,” says Nico, “it will slash fighters’ rights by enveloping them in a monolithic corporation. I feel obligated to protect the sport of boxing.” Note: since this article went to press in SPIN’s beautiful, tactile, unmissable print edition, Nico dropped his opposition and now champions the Muhammed Ali American Boxing Revival Act in revised form, although many others remain opposed. top.title: Alex Highsmith’s Status Revealed vs. Broncos
top.description: Pittsburgh Steelers outside linebacker Alex Highsmith in a game against the Atlanta Falcons on Sept. 13, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now PITTSBURGH — Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy revealed on Monday that outside linebacker Alex Highsmith is unlikely to suit up on Friday against the Denver Broncos. Highsmith suffered a left ankle injury in the first quarter of Sunday’s loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. “It’s going to be tough for him to make it this week,” McCarthy said. Highsmith suffered the injury after sacking quarterback Joe Milton in the first quarter. Highsmith was downgraded to out after initially being ruled questionable to return. Highsmith was in a boot after the game. Coming into Sunday’s game, Highsmith had 19 combined tackles (8 solo, 11 assists), 3.5 sacks, five tackles for loss, nine quarterback hits and one pass defended this season. Highsmith was all over the field before going down with an injury, recording two sacks and one QB hit. Highsmith forced a fumble on his first sack, but Eagles left tackle Jordan Mailata came up with the loose ball. KJ Henry , making his Steelers debut, replaced Highsmith at outside linebacker. Jack Sawyer also got reps. With Nick Herbig (ribs/hip) ruled out for Sunday’s game, the Steelers signed Henry to the active roster off the practice squad. Herbig could also be out on Friday, as well. McCarthy said Herbig is still in the rehab practice group. Brendan Howe provided reporting from Pittsburgh. nigeria.title: Delta govt imposes curfew in Ughelli North after campaign rally violence
nigeria.description: The Delta State Government has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew in Ughelli North Local Government Area following reported violence at a campaign rally of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in Uduere Community, which allegedly left some people dead and several others injured. The curfew, which takes effect from 6:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. daily, will remain in force until further notice. The Delta State Police Command disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday by its Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bright Edafe. According to the statement, the police have commenced investigations to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify those responsible. The Command urged residents to comply strictly with the curfew and cooperate with security personnel to maintain peace and public safety. The statement reads, “The Command therefore urges residents of Ughelli North Local Government Area to comply strictly with the curfew imposed by the Delta State Government, restricting movement between 1800hrs to 0600hrs until further notice. Residents are advised to remain calm and cooperate with security personnel in the interest of public safety. “The Commissioner of Police, Delta State Command, CP Samuel E. Erale, psc, mnips, has directed intensified security operations in the affected area to prevent further violence and maintain law and order. The CP has ordered a full-scale investigation and assures residents of the state that anyone found culpable will face the full weight of the law, irrespective of political affiliation or status, and urges members of the public to provide credible information to assist ongoing investigations.” Erale also extended his condolences to the families of those who died and wished the injured a speedy recovery. He reaffirmed the Command’s commitment to protecting lives and property while ensuring a peaceful environment for lawful political activities. The police commissioner further warned political actors and their supporters against thuggery, intimidation and the unlawful use of firearms. He stressed that political differences must never be allowed to degenerate into violence or loss of lives. nigeria.title: 89 fall ill after unknown substance released at UK Arena concert
nigeria.description: Thousands of concertgoers were evacuated from the UK’s largest indoor arena after the release of an “unknown substance”, with dozens reporting suffering side effects, police said Monday. Some 12,000 people were attending the Sunday night show by US rapper Don Toliver at the Co-op Live arena in Manchester, northwest England. “A total of 89 people displayed symptoms believed to be linked to exposure,” Manchester police said, adding one woman was taken to hospital for treatment. “Enquiries remain ongoing to establish the nature of the substance, where it came from and any associated risk,” Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding said in a statement. Toliver said he had postponed his Monday night London show following the incident, which led to one person being taken to hospital. Emergency services were called after “reports of people in the crowd suffering effects from an unknown substance”, Manchester police said, declaring a major incident at the scene. The venue, which bills itself as the country’s largest live entertainment arena, said it was working with police to “identify the cause of the incident”. The regional ambulance service said it assessed more than 50 people, including some reporting “eye and respiratory symptoms”. Toliver, who was nominated for five Grammy Awards last week, is currently on the second leg of his “Nitrous” world tour. He announced he was rescheduling his show at London’s O2 arena due to an “unfortunate incident last night (in) Manchester”. “My heart and prayers are with everyone that was injured last night,” Toliver said on Instagram, without providing more details. Concertgoers told the BBC that people were “choking” and coughing, recalling “distressing scenes” of people leaving the venue in a panic. Some criticised the lack of security checks at the venue, especially in a city still scarred by the 2017 Manchester Arena bombing, which killed 22 people at an Ariana Grande concert. nigeria.title: 2027: Armed Men Who Killed Four NDC Campaign Members Said I Was Their Target, Omo-Agege
nigeria.description: Former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege has alleged that the gunmen who attacked his campaign team in Delta State, killing four people, repeatedly shouted his name and declared their intention to kill him. Omo-Agege, who is seeking election to the Delta Central Senatorial District on the platform of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the 2027 general elections, said he escaped the attack through the intervention of his Department of State Services (DSS) escorts. He spoke on Monday while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s Politics Today . ﻿ Recounting the incident, the former deputy senate president said he heard the attackers repeatedly shouting that they wanted to kill him while opening fire at the campaign venue. “Right there at the venue, while they were shooting, we could hear them say, ‘It is Omo-Agege we want to kill. We must kill Omo-Agege.’ “But I was lucky because my DSS details were very professional. In fact, after God, the only reason I am alive today is because of the DSS operatives who were with me,” he said. Omo-Agege described the incident as a premeditated attack, alleging that there had been a build-up to the violence. He questioned why he would be singled out for elimination when several other politicians were also contesting elective positions. The former lawmaker said the attackers struck less than five minutes after he began addressing supporters at the campaign venue. According to him, he had moved towards the side of his vehicle to make eye contact with members of the audience when the gunshots rang out. “It was by divine intervention. As I was speaking, I just moved over to the side of the vehicle to be able to make eye contact with those I was speaking with. It was immediately I did that that the volley of gunshots started,” he said. The former deputy senate president said four members of his campaign organisation were killed, while about 15 others sustained injuries, with some in critical condition. ﻿ In a statement issued earlier on Monday by his media adviser, Sunny Areh, Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation said he survived an assassination attempt during a campaign tour in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. Areh alleged that armed men opened fire on the senator and his entourage while he was addressing supporters during a campaign visit. The organisation called for an independent and thorough investigation by the Nigeria Police Force, while appealing to the Inspector-General of Police, the DSS, INEC, civil society organisations and the international community to ensure the safety of political candidates and their supporters. It also urged supporters to remain calm and avoid retaliation, adding that its ward-to-ward campaign activities across Delta Central would continue. nigeria.title: Caregiver Salami shot dead in US weeks before starting Nursing school
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye A 24-year-old Togolese caregiver in Chicago, Bintou Salami, has been shot dead while returning home from work, weeks before she was due to begin nursing school. According to ABC7 Chicago, Salami was found with a gunshot wound in the 1400 block of West Chase Avenue at about 11:15 p.m. on Wednesday. She had just finished her shift at Misericordia, where she cared for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Ms Salami relocated from France to the U.S. in 2024 following her marriage and planned to begin nursing school in January; she is survived by her husband and son. Her killing was one of three shootings on Chicago’s North Side that night as Police said the incidents were connected. A 35-year-old man was critically wounded near the bike path by Belmont Harbor, while a 25-year-old man was later found dead at the Morse Red Line station and a gun was recovered at the station. The Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office said the man died by suicide. Salami’s coworkers described her as caring and devoted. Ashley Hespen, assistant vice president of residential services at Misericordia, said residents loved spending time with her. Friends, relatives and members of Chicago’s Togolese community gathered at a vigil to honour Salami and demand answers. As they sang the Togolese national anthem, supporters stood with her brother at the place where she was killed. “I can’t stop looking at the picture. I don’t know, like — it’s not fair,” said Nanipo Damyete, Salami’s former roommate. Amevi Avouglah, the USA country delegate for the High Council of Togolese Abroad, said Salami’s future had been cut short. “All the dreams that Bintou is carrying vanished like that in one minute! She was coming from work,” Avouglah said. Salami’s brother, Raoufou, questioned the suggestion that she was killed during a robbery, saying nothing appeared to have been taken. “The police telling me, like, somebody tried to rob her or something. What I can’t understand is how are you trying to rob somebody and you don’t take her phone, nothing?” he said. Salami moved to the United States from France in 2024 after completing college and following her marriage. She is survived by her husband and their 4-year-old son, who lives with her mother in Togo. Chicago police have not publicly explained how the shootings were connected and no suspects have been identified. The fatal shooting has sparked calls for justice from her family, friends and members of the Togolese community in the U.S. Vanguard News The post Caregiver Salami shot dead in US weeks before starting Nursing school appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: PSG suffer major injury blow as Doue, Kvaratskhelia face long layoffs
nigeria.description: The sight of the unfortunate Desire Doue going down holding his knee in agony was distressing for anyone connected to Paris Saint-Germain, but encouraging for those hoping to stop the French club from winning a third consecutive Champions League this season. PSG have been European champions in each of the last two years and their quest to retain the crown this season has started superbly, with four straight wins leaving them top of the 36-team standings halfway through the league phase. However, they have now lost the outstanding Doue, exactly a month after Khvicha Kvaratskhelia succumbed to the same injury, casting serious doubt over the chances of Luis Enrique’s team going all the way again. Doue was stretchered off in tears after twisting his knee awkwardly during PSG’s 3-2 win at Nice in Ligue 1 on Saturday, with the club later confirming the 21-year-old had ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee and needed surgery. Doue’s season is likely now over, while Kvaratskhelia is beginning the process of rehabilitation after rupturing the same ACL in last month’s win over Barcelona. The explosive Georgian winger was the best player in last season’s Champions League knockout rounds and came sixth in this year’s Ballon d’Or ranking. Meanwhile Doue was the man of the match when Paris demolished Inter Milan 5-0 in the 2025 Champions League final and had been their star performer in recent weeks. “He will come back twice as strong. I am not worried,” insisted Luis Enrique, but he will know that the injuries to two of his best attacking players seriously damage the club’s prospects of more European glory. So what do they do now, as they prepare to host Roma on Wednesday and with the January transfer window approaching? “We are always open to possibilities in the transfer window, but not just because we have players injured,” said the Spaniard. “We have players who can come in and we will overcome this as a team. It is not a problem.” He could be forgiven for now regretting the decision to allow Bradley Barcola — scorer of 34 goals across the last two campaigns — to leave for Liverpool. Suddenly the pressure on the injury-prone Ousmane Dembele to stay fit is enormous. – Bayern in bother – As for who appears the best-placed to take advantage of PSG’s misfortune, it may not be Bayern Munich, as the German champions deal with problems of their own. Twenty-four hours before Doue went down for PSG, newly-crowned Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane was substituted with an ankle injury playing for Bayern against Cologne. He is now expected to be sidelined for up to four months, although that will at least mean he has a chance of being fresh by March, in time for the Champions League knockout rounds. “I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season,” Kane said in a social media post. nigeria.title: Sinner set to undergo knee surgery, might miss Australian Open
nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Former world number one Jannik Sinner is set to undergo knee surgery in Finland, a development that could rule him out of the 2027 Australian Open, according to Sky Sports Italia. The Italian tennis star could be sidelined for between three and four months following the procedure, which is expected to be performed by Lasse Lempainen, a specialist in tendon and muscle injuries. Sinner, 25, has been struggling with persistent inflammation in his right knee, which forced him to end his 2026 season prematurely. Despite competing in only nine tournaments during the 2026 season, Sinner recorded 44 wins in 47 matches, won six titles and reclaimed the world number one ranking during a 30-match winning streak. nigeria.description: Former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, has called on the Inspector-General of Police to take over the investigation into the alleged assassination attempt on him in Delta State, saying he has no confidence in the state police command to deliver justice. Omo-Agege, the Nigeria Democratic Congress senatorial candidate for Delta Central, made the appeal on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday, following an attack on his campaign entourage in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area. nigeria.title: Osun police bust child trafficking syndicate, rescue 16-day-old baby
nigeria.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Osun State Police Command has dismantled a suspected child trafficking syndicate and rescued a 16-day-old baby boy allegedly sold for N1.5 million in a transaction involving two suspects. The command’s Public Relations Officer, DSP Abiodun Ojelabi, disclosed this in a statement on Monday, saying two suspects had been arrested in connection with the alleged trafficking. According to the police, the baby’s mother, Victoria Michael, 18, gave birth at a private hospital in Kajola on November 2 but was unable to cater for the child after the father, identified as Tayo, allegedly denied responsibility. Ojelabi said one of the mother’s friends, Comfort Olayinka, offered to help her find assistance through a contact in Abeokuta, Ogun State. He said Olayinka subsequently linked up with Oladipo Olamide, 46, who allegedly claimed to operate a non-governmental organisation providing care for less-privileged persons and offered to take the baby into its care. The police spokesman said the baby’s mother and Olayinka travelled to Abeokuta on November 5 and handed the child over to Olamide. However, Olayinka later allegedly told the mother that the baby had died and gave her a folded object resembling a baby, packed in a bag, which she was instructed to throw into Lafenwa River. Unknown to the mother, Olayinka had allegedly collected N450,000 from Olamide, purportedly for her upkeep. Ojelabi said police operatives, acting on intelligence, arrested Olamide in Abeokuta on November 17. During interrogation, the suspect allegedly confessed to selling the baby to one Mrs Bolanle Ruth for N1.5 million. He said Olamide subsequently led the operatives to Akure, Ondo State, where Ruth was arrested on November 18. According to the police, Ruth admitted paying N1.5 million for the baby and claimed she was promised that the necessary documents would be provided by an agency, but had yet to receive them. The police did not disclose the whereabouts or status of the other suspect, Olayinka, in the statement. Meanwhile, the Commissioner of Police in Osun State, Ibrahim Zungura, warned individuals and groups against child trafficking, assuring residents that the command would not tolerate the crime. He urged members of the public to provide useful information to security agencies to help prevent child trafficking and protect vulnerable children. business.title: Solo Bitcoin Miner Wins $191,000 Block Reward With Just 11 TH/s
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Solo Bitcoin Miner Wins $191,000 Block Reward With Just 11 TH/s A solo miner running about 11 terahashes per second has mined Bitcoin block 977,057, collecting a reward of 3.1287 BTC, or about $191,000, on a machine that makes up roughly one-millionth of a percent of the network. The block was found through the solo service at CKpool on Sunday, Nov. 22, at about 7:54 a.m. ET. The reward is the 3.125 BTC subsidy plus about 0.0037 BTC in transaction fees, and it was worth roughly $191,000 at bitcoin’s price when the block landed. How the solo block played out The block holds 584 transactions. Its coinbase transaction pays 3.0661 BTC to a single address and 0.0626 BTC, about 2% of the reward, to a second output. That split matches the service’s 2% fee, which means the miner’s take is a little over $186,000. Con Kolivas, the developer behind CKpool, congratulated the miner on X, whose address he abbreviated as bc1q~zy9j. It matches the end of the address that received the payout. Kolivas called it the 323rd block found on the service and “yet another lucky one.” He said the miner had only about 11.1 TH/s of hashrate on a 3.47 TH worker. “A miner of this size has about a one in 1650 chance of solving a block in a year,” Kolivas wrote. The block was tagged to Solo CK on the mempool.space block explorer, and its coinbase carries the pool’s signature. CKpool describes itself as a service that lets miners go after full solo blocks without running their own node, since you cannot mine directly to a Bitcoin Core node. A recent run of solo wins Solo CK has found five blocks since Nov. 6, according to the explorer’s pool page . The most recent before this one was block 976,642 on Nov. 19, followed by blocks on Nov. 11, Nov. 7 and Nov. 6. Each paid between 3.13 and 3.15 BTC. Earlier this year, a different solo miner won block 943,411 on the same service on April 2, for about 3.139 BTC. In October, a FutureBit Apollo solo miner found block 973,262 and earned 3.154 BTC. Those wins are the exception. Most of the network’s hashrate sits in large pools and industrial operations that split rewards across many miners, which is how they smooth out the luck. A single small machine can run for years without finding anything, and a lucky block can show up on day one. Miners on the service get nothing unless they find a block, and then they keep the full reward minus the 2% fee. Network hashrate and difficulty Bitcoin’s network hashrate was about 1.04 zettahashes per second, or roughly 1,043 exahashes, on a three-day average Monday. At 11.1 TH/s, the winning miner contributes about 0.000001% of that total, which fits Kolivas’s odds. One in 1,650 works out to a chance of about 0.06% over a full year of mining. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? sports.title: Ex-Chelsea star defends Cole Palmer after criticism over reaction to Leeds loss
sports.description: Former Chelsea striker Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink has defended Cole Palmer ’s commitment after the forward faced scrutiny following Saturday’s 4-1 thrashing at home against Leeds. Palmer failed to score once again, leaving him with just a single goal across his last nine Premier League appearances during a difficult run for Xabi Alonso ’s side. The England outcast attracted attention after the defeat due to an apparent exchange of words with injured team-mate Joao Pedro near the dugout, while reports suggested the Chelsea playmaker did not acknowledge the frustrated home support at Stamford Bridge . However, Hasselbaink told talkSPORT : "No, I don’t think there is discontent. sports.title: 'My football hasn't changed' - Kevin De Bruyne responds to prospect of Man City being stripped of titles as Napoli star returns to the Etihad
sports.description: FBL-EUR-C1-NAPOLI-PRESSER - AFP Kevin De Bruyne insists the prospect of Manchester City being stripped of titles would not change how he views his decade at the Etihad Stadium. Back in Manchester with Napoli, the Belgian declared his love for City's owners and admitted "everybody plays on the limit" of the rules, as he prepares to face his former club in the Champions League on Tuesday. De Bruyne responds to title-stripping threat De Bruyne has insisted his achievements with City will not be tarnished if the club are stripped of titles following the Premier League's guilty verdict. City were found guilty in September of the majority of the financial charges against them, and are appealing the decision. Speaking at a press conference at the Etihad on Monday night, De Bruyne was asked about the possibility of losing honours such as the 100-point title of 2017-18. "It still doesn't change, my football hasn't changed. Of course, in life, there are rules but everybody plays on the limit, I'd say," he said. 'I've given my all' The midfielder, who won six Premier League titles during his 10 years at City, insisted that his legacy is secure. "I've given my all, that's not going to change in my mind, I don't think a lot of people would change in their mind how they view me as a player or how we played," he said. "But... Ah! Everybody has their own opinion, I guess, and how people [say] 'disgrace', I can't change anything about that." De Bruyne added that his relationships with team-mates were what he valued most. 'This is my club! I love the owners' The Belgian made it clear that his bond with City remains as strong as ever, despite the verdict. "And honestly I still... This is my club! I love the owners, I've talked about a lot of stuff outside of football, I've even spoken to Khaldoon [Al Mubarak] how to buy a club and everything," he said. "I've nothing but affection for this club and that will never change! Even now, the people who treated me for 10 years exceptionally, my family and everything, that's for me the most important and for me, that is it to be honest." Emotional Etihad return awaits De Bruyne will now face his old club on Tuesday, as Enzo Maresca's side look to end their slump . The 35-year-old also hit out at reports in the Italian press about his future, saying the coverage had led to unpleasant reactions towards his wife.

sports.description: Sean Sullivan is the x-factor in the most recent trade between the White Sox and Rockies. | ﻿(Photo by Norm Hall/Minor League Baseball via Getty Images) On November 19, the White Sox sent Luis Castillo and Davis Martin to the Colorado Rockies in exchange for left-handed pitching prospect Sean Sullivan and 17-year-old catcher Doug Veliz. Let’s break down the exchange and see what Chicago’s plans likely are. On a surface level, this is a better deal for the Rockies. Castillo is a veteran starting pitcher, with a 3.75 career ERA in 266 starts over the last decade. Martin is also an established starter, and 2026 was his career-best season for starts (28), innings pitched (146) and ERA (3.95). He spent the first half of the year as the ace of the White Sox staff, and finished with solid season-long numbers. Meanwhile, Sullivan was Colorado’s No. 10 prospect on MLB Pipeline’s 2025 rankings, making five major league starts in 2026 but was rocked to an 8.87 ERA. Veliz is a teenager whose total pro ball experience is 117 PAs in the Dominican Summer League. So, then, why would the White Sox trade two quality starting pitchers for two prospects, one of whom has already struggled in the big leagues and the other being about as inexperienced as you can get? Well, it’s pretty simple — the trade was a salary dump for Castillo. He’s entering his age-34 season, and struggled substantially in 2026. He had a 5.06 ERA for the Seattle Mariners when the White Sox acquired him at the trade deadline. He proceeded to be even worse for the Sox, posting an 8.42 ERA over six starts. Castillo finished the year with a 5.85 ERA, in 130 2/3 innings over 29 games (23 starts). He’s owed $22.75 million in 2027, with a vesting option for 2028, and was the most expensive player on the Sox payroll. sports.title: The Grandson of The Greatest: Nico Ali Walsh on Fighting, Loss, and Protecting the Ali Boxing Reform Act
sports.description: Nico Ali Walsh (center) testifies at a Senate Committee hearing on federal boxing laws in Washington, DC, April 2026. (Photo by Saul Loeb / AFP via Getty Images) “The nerves reach a peak right before the bell hits,” says Nico Ali Walsh , the bell signaling the suspension of assault laws. When it dings, he and another man are legally free to beat each other in the head and body as hard and fast as possible. It’s a family tradition. More from Spin: Zwan’s ‘Mary Star Of The Sea’ Gets Deluxe Vinyl Reissue Justin Timberlake Confronts His Legacy In Apple TV Doc Trailer Soundwalk Collective, Patti Smith Continue ‘Correspondences’ Nico’s granddad was, of course, the sweet science’s zenith—The Greatest!— Muhammad Ali . So, when a teenage Nico decided to try his hand in the ring, he had a very special oldtimer spurring him on. “We would always watch videos of my sparring,” says Nico. “Every time I didn’t want to keep going, he’d push me to keep going. He wanted me to keep fighting.” Nico was raised (and still lives) in Las Vegas, with Muhammad in the Phoenix area. “My first amateur fight was down the street from him [Ali]. He was sick at the time, so he didn’t make the fight,” says Nico. “The next day I went back to his house and said, ‘Poppy, I lost the fight.’ Then we had a conversation about how losing is an opportunity to come back even better. He motivated me,” says Nico, now 26 and fighting as a middleweight. The determined youngster turned pro at 21. Nico now has 17 pro fights, winning 13 and losing two, with a draw and a no contest. He fought the Thai boxer Kittisak Klinson last year in the Philippines’ iconic Araneta Coliseum, where, 50 years earlier, his grandfather and Joe Frazier fought the Thrilla in Manila. Nico Ali Walsh (at right) in the office with Billy Wagner, Madison Square Garden, 2022. (Photo by Williams Paul/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Another fight he has picked up from his grandpa is the Muhammad Ali Boxing Reform Act . Championed by the Greatest himself, the Act protects boxers’ interests and independence and works against fixed contests, not allowing companies to simultaneously manage fighters, promote fights, and control the ranking and title system. Now, however, a new proposed law disingenuously titled Muhammad Ali American Boxing Revival Act is being pushed by Dana White, whose UFC juggernaut operates as an enclosed system in which fighters lack the independence of boxers. Dead opposite to what Muhammad Ali helped make law. “It’s absolutely horrible for boxing,” says Nico, “it will slash fighters’ rights by enveloping them in a monolithic corporation. I feel obligated to protect the sport of boxing.” Note: since this article went to press in SPIN’s beautiful, tactile, unmissable print edition, Nico dropped his opposition and now champions the Muhammed Ali American Boxing Revival Act in revised form, although many others remain opposed. sports.title: The Monday Perspective is thankful
sports.description: It is good to express gratitude and recognize things to be thankful for. Here is my non-exhaustive list of things I am thankful for when it comes to Gopher athletics. Truthfully, I could stop after the first two and be perfectly content. Holding all three rivalry trophies! For many Gopher fans, this is the first time in their lifetimes when the Little Brown Jug, Paul Bunyan’s Axe and Floyd of Rosedale are three housed in the Minnesota trophy case. Friday night is an opportunity to win them all in the same season and beat the Badgers for the fifth time in six seasons. There have been a couple of significantly disappointing games this season, both in the state of Indiana. But winning in Madison to complete the trifecta of beating Michigan, Iowa and Wisconsin in the same season would more than make up for those disappointments. There was some meat left on the bone this season, but if at the beginning of the season you would have told me 7-5 with wins over Michigan, Iowa and Wisconsin…I’d be pretty pleased. Niko Medved It is easy to be thankful for Medved right now as he has Gopher basketball undefeated and is generating a little buzz around the program. Anyone noticing what @GopherMBB is doing? Trounced Oklahoma State to improve to 7-0 and No. 21 on KenPom. @coachNikoMedved is cooking! — Seth Davis (@SethDavisHoops) November 23, 2026 This is the most competitive Gopher hoops squad since before the pandemic and maybe more importantly, they are truly enjoyable to watch. How this team moves the ball, plays together, and defends has been a treat. They have handled their early-season tests so far and they are in a great position to go undefeated in the non-conference portion of the schedule. Is there a chance that the Gopher offense can score more than 25 points on a regular basis next year? I’m thankful that it is at least a realistic possibility. sports.title: Final Thoughts on Penguins Road Trip and Why It Matters
sports.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It was not an easy road trip. The Pittsburgh Penguins faced a pair of teams on back-to-back days with a combined 25 wins, and now 27. Fresh from the wreckage of continued unacceptable unraveling performances, the Penguins face swirling trade talk of an imminent nature and a playoff race replaced with trying to avoid being the worst team in hockey. While the Penguins lost both games in regulation, first to the Nashville Predators 4-3 and then to the Dallas Stars 1-0, the games marked improvement. The Penguins weren’t good against Nashville, but neither did they suffer their recent implosions. And Sunday, the Penguins were quite good and largely outplayed Dallas but couldn’tget that shot or the extra bounce past Dallas goalie Jake Oettinger. But the road trip served to show a few things within the Penguins team. First, and perhaps as important as anything else, the team has not quit on itself. There have been many, MANY teams facing the end who surrender to the situation and are lifeless, listless, and barely present. The Penguins are certainly not going that route. CROSBY They have more struggles ahead, but rallying for themselves was important. They can indeed play something akin to disciplined, professional hockey, and they have some talent, albeit not an overwhelming amount, especially without Evgeni Malkin in the lineup . Of course, their talent level is likely to drop after the trades begin, but the players have a chance to rescue some pride as well as up their trade values. **The second thing that matters is the competent play of the under-25 players. And that factor has a couple of benefits, not the least of which is the effect on the trade talks. In the Venn diagram of the trade bait players and the young players, there is an issue that overlaps. As the veterans submit better performances, their value goes up, but also general manager Kyle Dubas can breathe a little easier knowing the players arriving from Wilkes-Barre/Scranton can adequately fill spots and the situation will not fall apart. In fact, that might be the most important takeaway from the weekend. The situation shouldn’t become a dumpster fire if and when Dubas begins dealing. The losses put the Penguins in next-to-last in the NHL; they’re already losing with the veterans, so there is no incentive to keep this course. **The young players are clearly seizing their opportunity, but also still growing into the league. Coach Dan Muse elevated Avery Hayes to the second line Sunday. While too much shouldn’t be made of the move because the previous night’s inhabitant, Andrei Kuzmenko, had a couple of bad turnovers and again struggled to assert himself after a first-period goal, Hayes’s placement also signaled that the team was giving a young player a chance. After all, Hayes wouldn’t ordinarily be the first choice for second-line duty, even without Nick Robertson and Evgeni Malkin in the lineup. Also, the under-25 set has been playing well. Hendrix Lap

technology.description: “It costs what it costs” is a mindset I’ve found useful when encountering a sizable, but highly necessary or desired, expense. Surveillance pricing leverages data collected from our web history , smart devices , and apps with the goal of getting us to pay more. technology.description: Western intelligence officials worry that Russia could launch a nuclear-armed satellite into orbit before the end of the year, suggesting the country's development of a satellite-killing weapon of mass destruction is more advanced than previously thought, German media reported Monday. The orbiting nuclear weapon would threaten thousands of satellites in low-Earth orbit, including military and commercial communications networks like Starshield and Starlink. A nuclear-armed satellite would also put at risk Western military surveillance satellites and human spaceflight platforms like the International Space Station. A nuclear detonation in orbit would be indiscriminate, also knocking out Russia's own spacecraft and Chinese satellites. US lawmakers briefed on government intelligence first disclosed Russia's ambition to deploy a space-based nuclear weapon in early 2024 . At the time, US officials said Russia had launched a test satellite in 2022 to test the effects of radiation on space hardware and pave the way for a future nuclear-armed craft, but that Russia had not yet sent a nuclear weapon into orbit. Sports in space have a long and proud tradition, whether it's Alan Shepard playing golf on the moon or the crew of the ISS hosting their own version of the Summer Olympics . The future looks bright as well, with the foundation of the Space Games Federation , the self-described "first governing and sanctioning body for competitive sports played in zero or micro-gravity," co-founded by a NASA astronaut. Not to be outdone, science fiction has expanded the idea of zero-g and low-gravity sports to their logical extent, imagining everything from Doctor Who's zero-g squash to the advanced, gamified combat simulations of Ender's Game. There was even Space Jam 's alien basketball game for the fate of the planet, though the gravity-defying antics there come from cartoon shenanigans rather than a zero-g playing field. As humanity edges closer to colonizing our neighbors through projects like the Artemis Program and its ambition to establish habitats on the moon, our imaginations have to expand to encompass not only how we'll live in space but also how we'll play. The rules change when gravity disappears (Image credit: Zero-G) We rarely think about it in an Earth context, but every sport is heavily influenced by gravity. It defines how balls arc, how quickly players can move, and even how we orient ourselves in play spaces. Remove the gravity, and all of those assumptions and mechanics evaporate as well. "First of all, in zero g, Isaac Newton will win every time," Les Johnson, former Chief Technologist for NASA, told Space. Les is a physicist with over 35 years of experience working at Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, as well as a science fiction author. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 23, 2015: Blue Origin sticks 1st-ever rocket landing from space with its suborbital New Shepard rocket
science.description: null On Nov. 23, 2015, a Blue Origin rocket made a historic landing. Before this time, all rockets were single-use only — even SpaceX's rockets. Blue Origin changed the concept forever. After launching the New Shepard capsule safely into space, the rocket started heading back to Earth. It flew towards a landing pad, reignited its engine to slow down and touched down softly on the ground . This was the first successful vertical landing from space in history. The Blue Origin milestone meant that rockets could be reused for multiple missions, which saves money and reduces waste. (Image credit: Blue Origin) Why it mattered Today, SpaceX may be the most well-known for landing its Falcon 9 rocket boosters from orbit. The company's triple-core Falcon Heavy boosters can also land vertically and its massive Starship megarocket can even return to the launch site to be caught by giant metal arms. But in the end, Blue Origin did it first. Blue Origin's New Shepard booster landing kicked off an era of vertical launch and vertical landings for rockets that continues to this day. It may have even outlasted the New Shepard rocket. Since that first landing, Blue Origin has launched 17 suborbital astronaut flights with New Shepard, and 21 more uncrewed flights for a total of 38 missions between April 2015 and 2026. The company reused its New Shepard boosters repeatedly (though it did lose one during an uncrewed launch after a technical issue.) But in January 2026, the company announced a pause in New Shepard flights for two years so that it could focus on moon lander projects. But Blue Origin did not abandon rocket landings. Indeed, the company's success with New Shepard led it to build vertical landing into its larger orbital rocket, New Glenn, which made its first successful landing 2025 — nearly 10 years after that first touchdown. Blue Origin has since reflown a New Glenn booster , and is developing a new rocket engine called Northstar for even better performance. Want more space history? science.title: The remains of a long-dead volcano on Mars | Space photo of the day for Nov. 23, 2026
science.description: null An image of Tharsis Tholus, a volcano on the surface of Mars, produced by ESA's Mars Express orbiter. (Image credit: ESA/DLR/FU Berlin) Researchers have spotted an ancient, "dead" Martian volcano from orbit around the Red Planet. What is it? The European Space Agency's Mars Express spacecraft, which has been orbiting and studying the planet since it arrived in 2003, recently captured incredible new imagery of the volcano Tharsis Tholus. This snapshot was captured by the spacecraft's High Resolution Stereo Camera. Even as old and worn as it is, the Martian volcano stands at around 4.97 miles (8 kilometers) tall which is comparable to some of the highest peaks in the Himalayan mountains. Despite its impressive height, it's still only about a medium-sized volcano for Mars, which is home much more impressively-sized volcanoes. For example, the planet's largest volcano Olympus Mons measures in at roughly 13.2 miles high (21.3 kilometers). Tharsis Tholus, a volcano on the surface of Mars, as seen by ESA's Mars Express orbiter. (Image credit: ESA/DLR/FU Berlin) Why is it incredible? While Tharsis Tholus might not be the tallest volcano on Mars, it is incredibly steep. It is steeper than Mauna Kea in Hawaii on Earth. To fully showcase the volcano's structure and topography in 3D, researchers actually exaggerated the vertical scale in this image, ESA reported . In addition to being steep and fairly tall, the volcano also has an interesting history. You can see that it is speckled with what look like small holes which are actually craters created by impacts from objects like asteroids. The volcano's current, unique shape is a combined effort by these impacts, environmental factors causing erosion and warping and ancient lava flows that left behind built-up material. The observations by Mars Express also reveals cracks and other imperfections in the volcano. All of these details might seem like superficial bits of detail, however every small crater, every lumpy cliffside and every worn down surface hides information about the planet's past. By studying features like volcanoes on Mars, researchers can piece together what the planet may have looked like in its ancient past. How active was this volcano? How did it interact with the landscape around it? Observations like this can hold the answers.

science.title: COP31 collapse has shattered the pretence of a global climate consensus
science.description: A closing plenary session at the COP31 climate summit on 22 November AP Photo/Khalil Hamra/Alamy A deep rift among nations on how to tackle climate change, and whether the global economy can be weaned off fossil fuels, was exposed after the spectacular collapse of talks at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey. After a tortuous fortnight of negotiations, COP31 ended in disarray late on 22 November after countries including the UK and the EU refused to agree to a political accord that failed to mention fossil fuels. Read more Can everyone live a ‘good life’ without destroying the planet? The Antalya pact would have seen countries officially recognise that the world is on course to exceed 1.5°C degrees of warming and promise to limit the scale of the overshoot as far as possible. It also would have committed nations to increasing the share of electricity in total final energy consumption to 35 per cent globally by 2035, a key target for climate campaigners who see electrification as the route away from fossil-fuel dependency. Advertisement But the draft agreement proved unacceptable to many countries, including the UK, the EU and some small island nations, after all mentions of fossil fuels were omitted at the behest of fossil fuel-dependent nations such as Saudi Arabia and Russia. Failing to mention fossil fuels explicitly in the text would have marked a backwards step for the climate process, the EU argued. At COP28 in Dubai three years ago, nations agreed to “transition away from fossil fuels” , but since then, attempts to strengthen the language or clarify how this transition will take place have been blocked by petrostates. Alden Meyer at the climate think tank E3G says the talks were subjected to a “brutish” strategy from fossil fuel-exporting states to “systematically block” any reference to the COP28 deal. “They clearly have buyer’s remorse about that agreement. They never were happy about it.” Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter The EU also took issue with a paragraph inserted at the behest of Saudi Arabia – which leads the 22-member Arab group of countries – calling for the rapid growth of carbon capture and storage technologies to the gigatonne scale by 2035. Carbon capture and storage technologies are expensive and unproven at scale, and many sceptics are concerned that focusing on them will justify the continued use of fossil fuels and distract from the deep emissions cuts necessary for controlling climate change. Ireland’s climate minister Darragh O’ Brien, speaking on behalf of the EU, claimed the negotiations had been “hijacked by fossil fuel producers” and said the EU would “not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuels”. Micah Hanks is a science reporter and podcaster focusing on space and astronomy, and Editor at TheDebrief.org. Follow him on X @MicahHanks.

On July 12, 1988, Phobos 2 — one of the Soviet Union's final major planetary exploration probes — was launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome aboard a Proton rocket. The spacecraft's mission included the study of Mars and the Martian moon Phobos, with a planned close approach and deployment of landing probes, and over the next several months, the spacecraft successfully captured more than three dozen images of Phobos during its time in service. However, early in the following year, the spacecraft's mission abruptly ended after the Phobos 2 ground team mysteriously lost contact with the spacecraft. Adding to the mystery were objects in some of the final photographs dispatched by the doomed spacecraft, which seemed to show an elongated shadow beneath the probe — a strange twist in one of the Soviet Union's final space missions, and one that soon gave rise to conspiracy theories about what the fate of Phobos 2 might have been. So what caused the odd-looking appearance of the shadow in the final images captured by Phobos 2, and what was the real reason behind the spacecraft's sudden failure? Last of the Soviet space explorers Originally, the Soviet Union had planned for Phobos 2 to reach the Red Planet by late January 1989, after which the spacecraft would begin collecting data about the Martian environment leading up to its initial contact with Mars' largest moon in early June. science.title: Astronomers just discovered a rare triple star system 28 light-years away, and they have ‘no clean explanation for how it got here’
science.description: A triple system containing a dim red dwarf star and not one but two white dwarfs has been fortuitously discovered just 28 light-years away from our solar system. "We were actually looking for planets ," Étienne Artigau of the Trottier Institute for Research on Exoplanets at the Université de Montréal, who led the discovery, said in a statement . "Instead, we found something much more surprising." So surprising that there are no similar systems within at least 100 light-years . Furthermore, the configuration of the system seems impossible. "This system should not exist," added Montreal's Patrick Dufour. "We have no clean explanation for how it got here." This triple system has been called Welopō'ai, which is a portmanteau of two Hawaiian words that means a 'path of family traits', and to understand the mystery behind it requires astronomers to figure out the history of the three objects. A white dwarf is what remains when a star of similar mass to our sun reaches the end of its life. As it begins to run low on hydrogen for nuclear fusion reactions in its core, the star's energy generation begins to falter and its interior starts to contract under gravity . This has the effect of raising the temperature throughout the star, causing an outer shell of hydrogen to ignite its own fusion reactions. The star promptly bloats to become a red giant tens or even hundreds of millions of kilometers across. Soon enough the star ceases fusion reactions completely. The star's outer layers are shed and they expand out into space, while its core contracts to become an inert white dwarf with a diameter similar to Earth but with a mass generally between half and two-thirds of a solar mass . Therefore, the Welopō'ai system was once a triple system with two sun-like stars plus the red dwarf. Now the two sun-like stars have undergone this stage of star death while their companion red dwarf continues to linger, since its low mass bequeaths it a longer life because it does not use up its core hydrogen as quickly. One of the white dwarfs orbits the red dwarf at a distance of 129.3 astronomical units (19.3 billion kilometers or 12 billion miles) and takes about 1,000 years to complete one orbit. This white dwarf and the red dwarf were previously known, and Artigau's team had been using the SPectropolarimètre InfraROUge (SPIRou) instrument on the Canada–France–Hawaii Telescope atop Mauna Kea to search for planets orbiting the red dwarf when they noticed something highly unusual. NASA Earth Observatory/Lauren Dauphin More than 60 years ago, scientists at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center aimed a laser skyward and fired a pulse of light at an orbiting satellite equipped with special reflectors. By measuring the time it took for the light to return, they demonstrated a new, more precise method for tracking satellites. Since then, satellite laser ranging (SLR) has grown more precise and more widely used. The technique now underpins many aspects of Earth observation, such as validating satellite orbits and mapping subtle changes to Earth’s surface. Pioneered at the Goddard Optical Research Facility—now the Goddard Geophysical and Astronomical Observatory —laser ranging is performed at more than 40 stations worldwide. In 2026, the next generation of SLR, developed by NASA scientists and tested at Goddard, began to come online. On October 12, a faster, even more precise SLR system officially debuted at the Ny-Ålesund Geodetic Observatory in Svalbard, Norway, operated by the Norwegian Mapping Authority, a NASA partner. It is the first NASA next-generation SLR system in operation and the northernmost SLR facility on Earth. While the systems developed decades ago have been “workhorses” of the global laser tracking network, their age and the growing number of satellites have necessitated updates, said Stephen Merkowitz, project manager for NASA’s Space Geodesy Project . “We wanted newer systems that could track more objects, and track them more accurately and precisely,” he said.
